## What exists (high level; details in `01-architecture.md`)

Config and profiles; IDs, events, ledger; headless run wrapper; preflight and 3-source kill switch; guard hooks and role tool lists; state branch; Notion layer (bootstrap, map, mirror, outbox, value-based conflicts); `init`, `status`, `pause`; orchestrator agent v0; 58-artifact catalog with 28 draft templates; live test tier; four judge reviews in `docs/process/reviews/`.

Not built: everything in Stages 1 to 5, including the eight other agents, the state machine, dispatcher, merge/publish scripts, digest, cost, gates, meetings, sandbox.

## Orientation

If you are new: `CONCEPT.md` first. ARIMA is a replica of a company software team (roles, gated phases, 58 owned artifacts, scheduled communications, measured cost and time) that builds a greenfield web app; the code in this repo is the machine that carries that team. The plan was re-checked against this concept on 2026-11-19: question and decision protocol moved to Stage 1 (WP-141), and packages were added for delivery metrics (WP-132), milestone review and retro (WP-217), QA authoring (WP-315) and the Phase 0 playbook (WP-321). `artifact-map.yaml` assigns every artifact to a builder.

## Decisions made on 2026-11-19 (see `09-owner-decisions.md`)

The owner steers by commands, answers only critical-blocker questions and reviews results; agents collaborate without asking permission. Tech-lead approves ADRs; baseline freezes on approval; `/arima:run` covers Phase 4 and operations only; hosting is local Docker Compose with GitHub Actions CI (reference stack in ADR-0007); no role holds a GitHub token (the host posts comments, pushes, merges, tags); no AI attribution in any commit or PR. All open questions in the agent cards and feature specs are resolved under these principles.

4. WP-102 is done: `src/packet.ts` (`renderPacket`, `validatePacket`, `parsePacket`, `forbiddenInput`) and `arima-packet render|validate` (exit 0/2/20). Untrusted text, including its label, is only ever inside `untrusted` fences (fence longer than any backtick run in the text); the dispatcher (WP-120) supplies the PacketInput. Over the 40,000-character cap, blocks that have a path are listed by path instead of inlined.
5. WP-103 is done: `src/report-collector.ts` (`extractReport`, `collectReport`) and, in `run-agent.ts`, the `kind` option and `runUnit()` (retry once with `min(per_run_cap, story remaining - spent)`, second failure or no budget = `blocked: true`; pauses, cap stops and refused dispatches are never retried). `arima-run-agent --kind <kind>` turns collection on; without it nothing changes. A bad report is `fail` with reason `report_invalid`, `evidence_missing` or `secret_in_output`; the ledger row carries `reason`; events `report.accepted`/`report.rejected`/`unit.retried`. The dispatcher (WP-120) must call `runUnit`, raise the question and set the item Blocked (WP-107/108), and make the fresh worktree in `beforeRetry`. G-06 fixed.

WP-104 is done: push binds each entry to its run (`run.start` event) and role, enforces `OUTBOX_DATABASES` (`roles.ts`, reason `database_not_allowed`) and forbidden properties (ba, ux: `Priority`), and accepts a created id-titled row only if `allocateId` issued the id to that run (`notion/allocations.ts`, `state/allocations.json`). `enqueueReportRecords` (`notion/proposals.ts`) turns a validated report's `records[]`, `questions[]`, `decisions[]` into entries with engine-issued ids and rewrites `NEW-n` placeholders. `pushOutbox` option `bindRuns: false` is for tests that push hand-made entries. Status opt-in is `{ idPrefix: 'init-' }` for init (G-02); outbox pattern is top-level `*.json` (G-07); one secret allow-list reader (G-09). Questions are enqueued without `Status` (WP-141 owns question state). The dispatcher (WP-120) must call `enqueueReportRecords` after `collectReport` accepts a report.

The dispatcher (WP-120) must pass `storyBudgetFromMirror(...)` for every story run and Block the item with a question on refusal. The 3x-median and rework alerts stay with WP-131.

The DoR needs `api_covered` and `open_dependencies` from the caller (WP-109 computes them); `attempt` starts at 1.
9. WP-107 is done: `src/state-machine.ts` (`transition`, `createMachine(table)`, `TRANSITIONS` = the 13 rows of contracts section 9, `afterRunFailure`, `MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS` 3, `MAX_RUN_FAILURES` 2). Pure: it returns `next` state, the `item.status` event and the engine-made Notion `Status` write, and applies nothing (WP-108 does). Check order: edge and actor, guards (all must be `true`; missing = false), hard stop (Blocked and Cancelled still allowed), budget (for In Progress, In Review, In QA). `attempt` starts at 1; the third review or QA failure redirects to Blocked (attempt 4, `redirected: true`, a question is due); a veto does not count as an attempt; Blocked returns only to `blocked_from`; any status change resets `run_failures`. `state-machine.test.ts` checks every (from, to, actor) against a separate copy of the spec table and 79 mutants of the table all fail it.
10. WP-108 is done: `src/item-status.ts` — `moveItem` (state machine, then counters, `item.status` event and an engine `Status` entry `st-<run>-<item>-<n>`), `reconcileStatuses` (a human edit of `Status` in the mirror is adopted and logged with actor `human`; pending engine writes, never-moved stories and junk values are skipped), `ENGINE_STATUS_PREFIX`. Push lets `Status` through only for entries registered as engine entries (`state/engine-entries.json`, `registerEngineEntry`), NOT merely for an id prefix: an agent can write any top-level outbox file, so the `init-` prefix alone (WP-104) was forgeable; init now registers its entries and the dispatcher must push with `{ idPrefix: 'st-' }` plus `init-`. Scope: stories only (types Story, Bug fix, Tech task, Spike); the Bugs database has its own status list. `moveItem` needs a `run.start` event for its run id (push binds entries to runs). It returns `applied.question` for the caller to raise (WP-141).
11. WP-109 is done: `src/queue.ts` — `planDay(input, limits, ranks)` returns `{ units, skipped }` in the spec order (`RANKS`: incident, broken_main, rework, qa_of_prs, test_cases, new_stories, recurring, docs_and_debt); only a Ready story with test cases and budget is started, limited by developer slots (WIP = developer count, at least 1), and not at all while `prsAwaitingHuman >= maxPrsAwaitingHuman` (ranks 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 continue); ties by PO priority, S before L, lowest id; one unit per item per day, except what one rank deliberately gives an item (an incident's triage and hotfix, two reviewers). `storiesFromMirror` builds `StoryFacts` from the mirror and the ledger. Inputs the dispatcher (WP-120) must supply: incidents, `ciRedOnMain`, `stagingSmokeFailing`, `prReady` per story (from the host's read of GitHub), recurring jobs, docs and debt units, `prsAwaitingHuman`. `--only` and the turn caps are WP-120. Mutation checked: swapping any two ranks, or dropping one, changes the plan the tests expect.
12. WP-110 is done: `src/worktree.ts` (`createWorktree`, `removeWorktree`, `listWorktrees`, `pruneWorktrees`, `branchFor`, `slugify`) and `arima-worktree create|remove|list|prune` (exit 0/1/2, host only, in no role list). Worktrees live in `../<repo>-wt/<branch>` with a registry file `registry.json` there (run id, creating pid; kept outside `.arima/` so it never reaches the state branch). Create refuses protected, odd or existing branches and existing paths, checks the tree is clean at the base commit, and supports a sparse checkout from a plain path list (QA gets `tests/`, `api/`, `package.json`, no `src/` or `docs/`). Remove kills given process trees, retries with backoff, falls back to deleting the folder, prunes, and keeps the branch unless asked. `pruneWorktrees` (for dispatcher start) removes worktrees whose creating process is dead and keeps the branch (unpublished commits). QA needs its own branch (`qa/<item>-...`) because git allows one worktree per branch. Verified on Windows; the Linux run is the CI matrix's job (not run here). WP-190 (Docker) will use a local clone instead.
13. WP-201 is done (ADR-0007: reference stack, local Docker).
